originalTitle: Democrats warn of ‘hollowed out’ leadership after army chief resigns amid clashes with Hegseth
summary: Sudden departure of Daniel Driscoll comes after Pentagon chief removed senior officers and blocked promotions, prompting warnings of a leadership crisis
content: A senior Senate Democrat accused Pentagon secretary Pete Hegseth of having “hollowed out” the army’s senior ranks after its top civilian leader resigned after months of internal clashes with Hegseth. No official reason was given for army secretary Daniel Driscoll’s departure after 18 months on the job, while thousands of US soldiers are deployed in the Middle East. In a statement on Monday night, White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said Driscoll had been “highly effective in advancing President Trump’s agenda”, citing his work on “readiness and lethality” and his role in Russia-Ukraine negotiations. Democrats and Republicans alike praised Driscoll’s leadership, but in a statement, Senator Jack Reed, the ranking member on the Senate armed services committee, said he did “not welcome” it. “It is far past time for President Trump to recognize the lasting harm that Pete Hegseth is inflicting on the Department of Defense,” Reed said. “In the Army alone, he has fired and blocked the promotions of dozens of senior officers without explanation, including Army Chief of Staff General Randy George and half of all four-star generals. “Secretary Hegseth is cultivating a culture where dissent is punished and competence is secondary to personal allegiance.” An army official told CBS News that Driscoll spoke with Trump about the “current state” of the army before submitting his resignation. NBC News, citing a source familiar with the matter, reported that in that conversation Driscoll raised concerns about the army’s transformation and readiness and about Hegseth’s blocking those efforts by firing the generals responsible for them. The public rupture traces back to April, when Hegseth forced out the army’s chief of staff, Gen Randy George, along with two other senior officers. George had worked with Driscoll on the army transformation initiative, an effort to shift the service toward drones and faster weapons acquisition based on lessons from the war in Ukraine. Driscoll later told Congress he considered George “a transformational leader” and said he went to George’s house the day he learned of the firing. Driscoll sought the help of JD Vance, a friend since law school, as tensions with Hegseth deteriorated, the Washington Post reported. Driscoll also told the Post then that he had no plans to leave his post. “I have no plans to depart or resign as the secretary of the army,” he said. Since George’s departure, the army has moved to scale back a drone unit he and Driscoll had championed, returning it to a conventional infantry role, CBS has reported. Hegseth also removed four army colonels from consideration for promotion to brigadier general, over objections from Driscoll and George. Driscoll’s exit adds to a string of senior departures under Hegseth, including navy secretary John Phelan, Southern Command chief Adm Alvin Holsey, and Gen Chris Donahue, who commanded US army forces in Europe and Africa. Sean Parnell, Hegseth’s chief spokesperson, had privately expressed interest in the army secretary post before it became vacant, the Hill has reported, and is among those reportedly under consideration to succeed Driscoll. “The Pentagon right now is in some cases rudderless, without leadership at the senior rungs of the uniform offices and even in the civilian offices,” Representative Jason Crow, a Democrat and former army ranger who serves on the House armed services committee, told reporters. “I’m gravely concerned about it.” Driscoll, an Iraq war veteran who worked in finance and technology before joining the administration, also served as a Trump-appointed negotiator in talks to end the Russian war on Ukraine. Neither the White House nor the Pentagon has said what Driscoll told Trump in their final conversation or how the president responded.
chineseTitle: 陆军参谋长因与赫格赛斯的冲突而辞职后，民主党人警告称领导层将被“掏空”
chineseSummary: 丹尼尔·德里斯科尔突然离职，此前五角大楼负责人罢免了高级官员并阻止了晋升，引发了领导力危机的警告
chineseContent: 一名资深参议院民主党人指责五角大楼部长皮特·赫格斯在陆军最高文职领导人与赫格斯发生数月内部冲突后辞职后，“掏空”了军队的高级官员。陆军部长丹尼尔·德里斯科尔在上任 18 个月后离职，但没有给出正式原因，而数千名美国士兵则部署在中东。白宫发言人安娜·凯利在周一晚上的一份声明中表示，德里斯科尔“在推进特朗普总统的议程方面非常有效”，并提到了他在“战备和杀伤力”方面的工作以及他在俄罗斯-乌克兰谈判中的作用。民主党人和共和党人都赞扬了德里斯科尔的领导才能，但参议院军事委员会高级成员参议员杰克·里德在一份声明中表示，他“不欢迎”。里德说：“特朗普总统早就该认识到皮特·赫格斯对国防部造成的持久伤害了。” “仅在陆军中，他就在没有任何解释的情况下解雇了数十名高级军官，并阻止了他们的晋升，其中包括陆军参谋长兰迪·乔治将军和一半的四星将军。赫格塞斯部长正在培养一种文化，在这种文化中，异议会受到惩罚，能力比个人忠诚更重要。”一名陆军官员告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，德里斯科尔在提交辞呈之前与特朗普谈论了军队的“现状”。 NBC新闻援引一位知情人士的话报道称，德里斯科尔在那次谈话中对军队的转型和战备状态以及赫格斯通过解雇负责这些行动的将军来阻止这些努力表示担忧。公开的决裂可以追溯到四月份，当时赫格赛斯迫使陆军参谋长兰迪·乔治将军和另外两名高级军官下台。乔治·H
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
